title: MSFS 2024 Marketplace: Huge Atlanta Upgrade & Default Scenery Comparisons!
description:
The Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 marketplace just exploded with an incredibly diverse set of releases this week, bringing a massive mix of high-fidelity international airliner hubs, unique regional fields, and stunning visual landmarks. Whether you enjoy challenging, low-visibility long-haul airliner routes, low-level VFR flying over hidden backcountry airfields, or upgrading your dark-hour atmosphere, this week's drop covers an incredible amount of ground.

In this comprehensive marketplace breakdown, we are putting the biggest new releases head-to-head against the default MSFS 2024 streaming engine to analyze the structural upgrades, terminal interior details, and night illumination overhauls to see which add-ons genuinely deserve a spot in your virtual hangar.

To make sense of this massive drop, we have organized the latest releases into two logical categories:

✈️ MAJOR US COMMERCIAL & REGIONAL GATEWAYS: We kick off with the heavy airliner tarmac, heading straight to the highly anticipated Atlanta International Airport (KATL) by OBX (Matteo Venzanis). We evaluate its incredible single-developer scale, animated SkyTrain, custom VDGS, and extensive night lighting, along with critical setup advice to avoid default scenery conflicts. Next, we journey to Kansas to check out Manhattan Regional Airport (KMHK) by MSFSceneryBuilders, before executing a side-by-side comparison of Modesto City-County Airport (KMOD) directly against the default MSFS 2024 streaming engine to see how the custom hangars and open interiors transform the airfield.

🇬🇧 UK GENERAL AVIATION & VFR SCENE: For the general aviation pilots, we cross the Atlantic to dive into Netherthorpe Airfield (EGNF) by Burning Blue Design. Located near Nottinghamshire, this historic grass strip features over 100 custom 3D objects, fully modeled restaurant and hangar interiors, an animated signal square, and static PA28/C152 aircraft—making it the ultimate challenging destination for tight, low-altitude VFR operations.

Are you going to be taking a heavy commercial jet liner down into Georgia, practicing your short-field grass arrivals over in England, or exploring regional fields? Let me know in the comments below: which of these packages is landing on your hard drive first?

If this structured marketplace breakdown helps you plan your next flight route, make sure to hit that like button and subscribe for weekly MSFS realism updates!

(Stay tuned to the channel as I'll soon be sharing my first VR flight experience inside MSFS 2024 using the Pimax Crystal Light!)
